title: END — Debrief / Hot Wash

fields.resolution: ENDEX. The emergency lights dim. The screens go dark. A soft chime sounds through the room. The facilitator stands and speaks: 'This concludes the exercise. Thank you for your full engagement. We will now begin the hot wash.'
finalState: The attacker's presence in the network remains undetected by operations.
The Airport Security Program (ASP) and PACS configuration have been exfiltrated.
The Domain Controller and AODB server were compromised 90 days ago.
All 340 employees' PII has been exposed.
The airport is operating under manual procedures, with no confidence in digital systems.
fields.hotWashTransition: Thank you, everyone. Put down your phones and radios. We will take ten minutes, then start the hot wash.
fields.hotWashMethod: 3-Up / 3-Down: three things that went well, three things that broke
hotWashQuestions: When you read '90 days' — what was your first reaction? When did you realize how bad it was?
Which decision was the hardest — and what ultimately drove your choice?
What would you have done differently if you had detected this at Day 1 instead of Day 90?
What investments or policies would have prevented or shortened this compromise?
How did you handle the tension between 'be transparent' and 'don't panic everyone'?
fields.facilitatorNote: Collect all ICS 201 forms and evaluator sheets before the break. Note that the team's risk assessment of 'monitor and contain' was the most common choice — expect strong discussion on its trade-offs.
